Saudi Arabia's benchmark index ended a sixth consecutive week in the red after falling 1.6%

Ateeq Shariff | Reuters News

Most Gulf stock markets closed lower on Thursday as tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz hit a wartime high, deadly strikes on Saudi airports widened the conflict and stalled US-Iran diplomacy offered investors little relief. T

Saudi Arabia's benchmark index ended a sixth consecutive week in the red after falling 1.6%, its biggest one-day decline since March. Saudi National Bank, the country's largest lender by assets, lost 3.1%. 

 In Abu Dhabi, the index lost 1.6%, while Dubai's main share index shed 1.7%.

Investors stayed cautious amid regional tensions and stalled diplomacy, according to Mahmoud Mashal, senior market analyst at VT Markets in Dubai. 

Reports of a possible resumption of attacks weighed on sentiment and cast doubt on US-Iran talks, he said, while repeated tanker strikes and disruption at major maritime chokepoints kept worries alive as traffic fell. 

Qatar's benchmark index sank to its lowest level since the pandemic-driven selloff of June 2020, closing down 2.2%. The biggest drag was a 2.9% slide in Qatar National Bank (QNB), the Gulf's largest lender. Post trading hours, QNB reported third-quarter net profit of 4.65 billion riyals ($1.28 billion), up from 4.43 billion riyals a year earlier. 

The Egyptian bourse was closed for a public holiday. 

  1. Saudi Arabia fell 1.6% to 10,376 
  2. Abu Dhabi dropped 1.6% to 9,801 
  3. Dubai declined 1.7% to 5,799 
  4. Qatar retreated 2.2% to 9,006 
  5. Bahrain eased 0.2% to 1,896 
  6. Oman added 0.1% to 7,832 
  7. Kuwait down 0.4% to 9,032

($1 = 3.6450 Qatar riyals) 

(Reporting by Ateeq Shariff in Bengaluru; Editing by Sonia Cheema, Aidan Lewis)
